articles.title: 把世界看成复杂系统｜从有限表征，到决策与行动
articles.description: 从复杂系统与有限表征出发，围绕当前主体、目标和场景构建局部决策空间，并通过行动与反馈持续修正认识。

articles.title: 智能系统、生态位与 Agent 网络

articles.title: 表征｜AI 能理解什么，取决于世界如何被表示
articles.description: AI 能理解和操作什么，不只取决于模型能力，也取决于现实被如何表征。

articles.title: Word、Excel、PPT：被忽略的基础设施
articles.description: 文档、表格与空间画布承载不同形式的共享表征；下一代基础设施需要让人和智能系统共同理解、维护和操作这些结构。

articles.description: 从白板与 Cognitive IR 到业务数字孪生，探讨多个主体如何共同观察、修改和操作同一个持续更新、可计算的世界。

articles.title: 从文档到可计算的认知资产
articles.description: 基于 Cognitive IR 的人机协作知识组织方式

articles.title: Cognito Atlas｜为复杂现实建立可共享的认知地图
articles.description: 对复杂环境进行稳定表达，形成可复用的认知底图。

articles.title: Decision Space｜将复杂问题转化为可收敛，可求解的决策空间
articles.description: 如何围绕场景和目标裁剪问题空间，并逐步收敛可行路径。

articles.title: 设备字段越加越多，为什么人和 AI 还是用不明白？
articles.description: 从不断增加的设备字段继续追问业务域、视角与使用目的，探索如何基于稳定表征生成适合当前问题的视图。

articles.title: 让 Agent 自动从图纸生成 BOM，为什么最后先重做了产品定义？
articles.description: 客户最初想让 AI 从图纸自动生成 BOM。重新识别需求本质之后，先梳理了六个标准型号的产品定义和参数-物料配置规则，做成小工具投入使用。技术部门反馈，对应工作效率提升约 25%—30%。

articles.title: 让 Agent 自动处理审批，为什么得先把“审批”拆开？
articles.description: 从审批流回到业务对象、状态变化与真正需要判断的节点，重新理解 Agent 应该自动化什么。

articles.title: 新生产力，需要怎样的生产关系？
articles.description: 从岗位替代到组织与产业分工重构。

articles.title: 复杂度不会消失，只会转移？
articles.description: 复杂度会转移，也可能因重复定义和不一致被复制、放大。通过上游建模与结构调整，减少整个系统需要处理的不必要复杂度。

articles.title: 企业数字化的终局，是业务的数字孪生
articles.description: 持续映射业务对象、状态、规则与关系，让人和智能体在同一个数字环境中接续工作。

articles.title: 数字化的本质，是提升复杂系统的治理能力
articles.description: 数字化真正改变的，不只是工作效率，而是组织能够感知、理解和治理多复杂的现实。

articles.title: 为什么企业 AI 落地，需要一张共享的业务地图？
articles.description: Agent 要在企业里稳定行动，缺的不只是上下文，而是一套可持续更新、可导航的数字环境。

articles.title: 从企业 OS 到产业 OS
articles.description: 从行业规则复用与上下游协作出发，建立能够支持人、AI 和企业持续调整分工的数字环境。

articles.title: 业务建模，本质是定义业务如何被表征
articles.description: 建模不是把现有流程画下来，而是在决定现实中的哪些差异进入数字世界，以及以什么结构存在。

articles.title: 系统已经这么多了，为什么还要靠群聊和共享Excel？
articles.description: 系统已经覆盖了不少业务，但跨系统的业务逻辑仍靠人补齐。理解这些人工工作，才能判断哪些需要完善系统，哪些适合引入 Agent。

articles.title: 软件的边界，不是业务的边界：为什么需要企业 OS
articles.description: 从软件边界、系统集成与交期变更出发，讨论如何围绕完整业务组织共同数字环境，并让 LLM、IM 与系统实现接续工作。

articles.title: 产品需求的本质，是业务与数字孪生之间的 Gap
articles.description: 从流程、报表、操作优化和 Agent 需求出发，识别业务所需能力与现有数字孪生之间的缺口，明确建设范围，并回到业务运行中验证效果。

articles.title: 从业务、产品到代码，三张可互算架构图
articles.description: 显式连接业务要求、产品能力与技术实现，让覆盖检查、需求识别和变更影响分析有共同依据，推动三方共同建设和维护数字孪生。

articles.title: 系统实施为什么变成了配置地狱
articles.description: 自定义字段、流程和权限降低了实现门槛，却把业务设计问题留给了客户。配置越来越多，谁在负责整体结构？

articles.title: 传统企业数字化里的隐形断层：谁来定义业务如何进入数字世界？
articles.description: 很多真正需求会在建模、设计和运行中逐步浮现，但传统企业里，业务方熟悉现实却未必能稳定定义它，软件方又通常只负责实现已有需求，中间因此长期缺少持续定义业务数字表征的角色。

articles.title: 让 Agent 读完所有群聊，就能知道项目进度吗？
articles.description: 群聊能够提供持续发生的信号，但项目进度依赖对业务对象、状态、关系与变化的稳定表征。

articles.title: 当我们说“让 AI 帮人完成任务”，到底在说什么？
articles.description: 任务有自己的来源和目标。理解它为什么存在，才能判断应该加速、重构还是取消，以及 Agent 应该承担哪一段工作。

articles.title: 设计 Agent 之前，先弄清任务从哪里来
articles.description: 从组织职能、业务要求与当前状态出发，识别具体任务，再依据职责和授权确定由谁承接。

articles.title: 企业 AI 落地为什么必须从业务开始：业务 → 组织 → 系统 → Agent
articles.description: Agent 能做什么，取决于业务是否定义清楚、组织是否明确分工，以及系统是否稳定承载这些结构。企业 AI 可以从局部开始，但不能跳过这些前置条件。

articles.title: 讨论哪里能用Agent之前，先重新理解职能和组织分工
articles.description: 从业务对象与职能出发，明确人、系统和 Agent 的分工边界。

articles.title: 为什么 Agent 做着做着就做不动了？
articles.description: 业务、产品和技术未消化的复杂度，最终都落到了 Agent 身上。

articles.title: 把 Agent Harness 放回数字化背景中理解
articles.description: 主体维护自己的认知，环境维护共享的现实，Harness 负责二者之间稳定的感知、理解与行动接口。

articles.title: Context Engineering：一场草稿纸管理工程
articles.description: 草稿纸是外挂工作记忆，业务对象与共享状态则需要由环境持续承载。Agent 需要多少记忆，也取决于数字世界已经替它承载了多少信息。

articles.title: 知识库“建起来”了，为什么 AI 还是解决不了业务问题？
articles.description: 建模方法论 01｜域 × 视角 × 分辨率

articles.title: Seeing the world as a complex system | From limited representation to decision and action
articles.description: Starting from complex systems and limited representations, construct a local decision space around the current actor, goal, and situation, and revise understanding through action and feedback.

articles.title: Intelligent systems, ecological niches, and agent networks
articles.description: Starting from functional boundaries and ecological niches, explore harnesses, changes to environments, collaborative networks, and self-improvement.

articles.title: Agents and environments need to be modeled together
articles.description: Start from interactions between actors and environments to judge which difficulties need stronger intelligence and which should be removed by reorganizing the environment.

articles.title: Representation | What AI can understand depends on how the world is represented
articles.description: What AI can understand and operate on depends not only on model capability, but also on how reality is represented.

articles.title: Word, Excel, PowerPoint: Overlooked infrastructure
articles.description: Documents, spreadsheets, and spatial canvases carry different forms of shared representation. The next generation of infrastructure must enable people and intelligent systems to jointly understand, maintain, and operate these structures.

articles.title: From shared representation to a computable world | From whiteboards and Cognitive IR to digital twins: How information moves from being understood to enabling action
articles.description: From whiteboards and Cognitive IR to business digital twins, explore how multiple actors can jointly observe, modify, and operate on the same continuously updated, computable world.

articles.title: From documents to computable cognitive assets
articles.description: Organizing knowledge for human–AI collaboration with Cognitive IR

articles.title: Cognito Atlas | Building a shared cognitive map of complex reality
articles.description: A stable representation of complex environments that forms a reusable cognitive base map.

articles.title: Decision Space | Structuring complex problems to converge on feasible solutions
articles.description: How to narrow the problem space around a scenario and goal, then progressively narrow down the feasible paths.

articles.title: Why did automating BOM generation from drawings first require redefining the product?
articles.description: The customer initially wanted AI to generate BOMs automatically from drawings. After reassessing the underlying need, we first clarified the product definitions and parameter-to-material configuration rules for six standard models, then built a small tool and put it into use. The technical department reported an improvement of approximately 25%–30% in efficiency for this work.

articles.title: What Relations of Production Do New Productive Forces Require?
articles.description: From job replacement to reshaping organizational and industry divisions of work.

articles.title: Complexity doesn’t disappear—it only shifts. Or does it?
articles.description: Complexity can shift, be duplicated, and grow through inconsistent definitions. Upstream modeling and structural changes can reduce the unnecessary complexity the whole system must handle.

articles.title: Enterprise digitalization should ultimately create a business digital twin
articles.description: Continuously map business objects, states, rules, and relationships so people and agents can continue one another’s work in a shared digital environment.

articles.title: The essence of digitalization is improving the governance capacity of complex systems
articles.description: Digitalization changes more than efficiency: it expands the range and complexity of situations an organization can perceive, understand, and govern.

articles.title: Why does enterprise AI need a shared Business Atlas?
articles.description: For agents to act reliably inside an enterprise, context alone is not enough. They need a navigable digital environment that can be updated continuously.

articles.title: From Enterprise OS to Industry OS
articles.description: Build a digital environment that supports ongoing changes in the division of work among people, AI, and enterprises, starting with reusable industry rules and collaboration across the value chain.

articles.title: Business Modeling is fundamentally about defining how business is represented
articles.description: Modeling is not simply drawing existing workflows. It decides which distinctions in reality enter the Digital World and what structures give them form.

articles.title: Why do businesses still rely on group chats and shared Excel files despite having so many systems?
articles.description: Systems already cover much of the business, but people still fill in the business logic across them. Understanding this manual work helps identify where systems need improvement and where agents are appropriate.

articles.title: Software boundaries are not business boundaries: Why an Enterprise OS is needed
articles.description: Explore software boundaries, integration, and delivery-date changes to examine how a shared digital environment can organize the business as a whole and connect work across LLMs, IM, and system implementations.

articles.title: Product requirements define the gap between the business and its digital twin
articles.description: Identify the gaps between business needs and the existing digital twin behind requests for workflows, reports, usability improvements, and agents. Define the scope of development and verify its effects in actual business operations.

articles.title: From business to code: Reasoning across three architecture models
articles.description: Explicitly connect business requirements, product capabilities, and technical implementation to provide a shared basis for coverage checks, requirements analysis, and change impact analysis, supporting joint development and maintenance of the digital twin.

articles.title: Why has system implementation become configuration hell?
articles.description: Custom fields, workflows, and permissions lower the barrier to implementation but leave business design decisions to the customer. As configurations multiply, who is responsible for the overall structure?

articles.title: The Hidden Gap in Enterprise Digitalization: Who Defines How Business Is Represented?
articles.description: Many requirements only become clear over time through modeling, design, and operation. Yet business teams understand reality without necessarily being able to define it consistently, while software vendors usually implement only requirements already articulated. The gap is a missing role that continuously defines the digital representation of the business.

articles.title: Can an agent understand project progress simply by reading every group chat?
articles.description: Group chats provide a stream of signals, but project progress depends on a stable representation of business objects, states, relationships, and change.

articles.title: What do we mean when we say “let AI help people complete tasks”?
articles.description: Tasks have their own origins and goals. Understanding why they exist provides a basis for deciding whether to accelerate, redesign, or eliminate them, and which part of the work an agent should undertake.

articles.title: Before designing an agent, understand where tasks come from
articles.description: Trace specific tasks to organizational functions, business requirements, and current states, then use responsibilities and authority to determine who can undertake them.

articles.title: Why enterprise AI must start with the business: Business → organization → systems → agents
articles.description: What an agent can do depends on whether the business is clearly defined, responsibilities are explicit, and systems reliably represent and maintain those structures. Enterprise AI can start within a limited scope, but it cannot skip these prerequisites.

articles.title: Before discussing where to use agents, rethink business functions and the division of work in organizations
articles.description: Start with business objects and functions to define the division of responsibilities between people, systems, and agents.

articles.title: Why do AI agents stall when put to work?
articles.description: Complexity left unresolved in business definitions, product design, and technical implementation ultimately lands on the agent.

articles.title: Understanding agent harnesses in the context of digitalization
articles.description: Actors maintain their own cognition, environments maintain shared reality, and the harness provides a stable interface for perception, understanding, and action between them.

articles.title: Context engineering: Managing AI’s scratch paper
articles.description: Scratch paper provides external working memory; business objects and shared state need to be maintained by the environment. How much memory an agent needs also depends on what its Digital World already holds.

articles.title: You’ve built a knowledge base. Why does AI still struggle with business problems?
articles.description: Modeling methodology 01 | Domain × perspective × resolution
